newsitem.title: UK: Mackie sees lower profits due sales setback.
newsitem.headline: Mackie sees lower profits due sales setback.

text.p: Engineering firm Mackie International Group Plc said on Thursday a continued worsening of sales in its key market would mean profit expectations for the current year being cut back.
"The severity of the setback in textile machinery sales will result in a reduction in profit expectations for the currrent year," it said in a statement.
"Group profitability in the second half is dependent on sales yet to be made and delivered before the year end," it added.

Despite the problems from this area of the business, which it said "will result in a reduction in profit expectations for the current year", Mackie said it was confident that it would make a strong recovery from what it called a temporary setback.
In all, the impact of the textile division's reversal of fortunes would probably mean that the area's 1997 turnover would be not more than 12 million stg, it added.
"In summary, this gives the prospect of 1997 turnover of over 30 million stg of which textile machinery would comprise less than 40 percent of total group turnover," Mackie said.

It explained a strong balance sheet with low gearing, along with growth in its environmental business and the benefits of a new foundry that it expects will boost sales in 1997, should also underpin its business.
It predicted foundry output would be worth 3.0 million stg in 1997 and saw the facility giving the firm a base on which to build strategic engineering alliances.
"The group is already in advanced negotiations with five major continental European customers," it added.
